findings.title: Nocturnal cmd.exe C2 shells — dual instances, different parents, 8-17 day persistence

peirce_chain.firstness: Two cmd.exe processes observed: PID 2476 (parent 1396, started 2018-08-21 01:41:51 UTC, running 17 days) and PID 7704 (parent 5984, started 2018-08-30 17:38:59 UTC, running 8 days). Both active at dump time 2018-09-07.
peirce_chain.secondness: cmd.exe is ephemeral — it runs commands and exits. Two instances from DIFFERENT parents (PIDs 1396 and 5984) persisting for 17 and 8 days is structurally impossible for legitimate usage. The first spawn at 01:41 AM UTC is a nocturnal operation timestamp — consistent with APT actors operating during target organization off-hours to avoid detection. The second spawn 9 days later from a DIFFERENT parent suggests either (a) a second C2 operator/tool accessed the system, or (b) the first beacon manager (PID 1396) was replaced by a new one (PID 5984). Both patterns indicate sustained, multi-session access to an AV server — a strategically critical target.
peirce_chain.thirdness: cmd.exe-based C2 persistence (T1059.003). The attacker used cmd.exe shells as persistent command channels on the AV server. Nocturnal timing + multi-day persistence + different parents = sustained interactive access, not scripted automation. Targeting the AV server specifically enables T1562.001 (Disable or Modify Tools) — the attacker can suppress detection signatures, whitelist malicious binaries, or disable real-time protection before deploying payloads across the domain. This IS a concealment technique: compromising the security infrastructure that would otherwise detect the compromise. Corroborated by F-002 (29-process injection) and cross-server correlation with VIGIA-REAL-SRL-ADMIN.

findings.carnegie_pattern: Strategic target selection — AV server compromise neutralizes the primary detection mechanism, enabling undetected operations across the enterprise
findings.devil_advocate: cmd.exe at 01:41 AM COULD be a legitimate scheduled maintenance task (AV signature updates, database maintenance). Two instances from different parents could be separate scheduled tasks. HOWEVER: (1) scheduled tasks produce ephemeral cmd.exe that exits after completion — they do NOT persist for 17 days; (2) two instances from DIFFERENT parents rules out a single scheduled task; (3) nocturnal timing on an AV server is suspicious even for maintenance — AV updates typically run via the AV management console, not raw cmd.exe; (4) concurrent 29-process injection (F-002) independently confirms compromise; (5) cross-server correlation with admin server (same framework) provides external corroboration.
findings.corroboration: CONFIRMED by F-002 (29-process framework injection). EXTERNALLY CORROBORATED by VIGIA-REAL-SRL-ADMIN (same framework, 31 RWX processes, PowerShell C2, confirmed MALICE). Two independent Volatility plugins (pslist + malfind). Cross-case corroboration across two servers.

habit_incongruence.confirmed_by: F-002 corroboration + cross-server correlation + nocturnal timing + persistence duration

findings.title: 29-process framework injection — same framework as admin server (T1562.001 AV targeting)

peirce_chain.firstness: 29 processes have PAGE_EXECUTE_READWRITE memory regions not backed by files on disk. Admin server in same network shows 31 processes with identical pattern.
peirce_chain.secondness: AV server elevated baseline: heuristic engines may produce 10-15 malfind hits (AV sandbox + JIT). 29 processes is ~2x the AV-elevated baseline. Margin is smaller than admin server (3-6x normal baseline) but still well beyond legitimate. CRITICAL: the admin server (VIGIA-REAL-SRL-ADMIN, separate investigation, different kernel base 0xf8032461e000 vs 0xf80001a06000) shows 31 RWX processes — the near-identical count (29 vs 31) across two different servers with different kernel bases confirms the SAME post-exploitation framework was deployed to both. This cross-server fingerprint eliminates the JIT/AV false-positive hypothesis: no legitimate software configuration produces near-identical RWX counts across different server roles.
peirce_chain.thirdness: Reflective DLL injection (T1055.001) at framework scale, specifically targeting the AV server (T1562.001). The attacker deployed the same post-exploitation framework to both the admin server and the AV server. Compromising the AV server is a deliberate concealment strategy: (1) disable real-time protection to prevent payload detection, (2) whitelist attacker tools in AV exceptions, (3) gain visibility into what the AV product detects across all domain endpoints, (4) suppress alerts that would reveal the compromise. This IS the concealment layer: compromising the security tool that would otherwise detect the framework injection. MALICE confirmed by concealment intent + cross-server framework fingerprint + scale.

findings.carnegie_pattern: Neutralization — disabling the opponent's detection capability before expanding operations
findings.devil_advocate: AV servers have elevated RWX baselines due to heuristic scanning engines. AV behavioral analysis allocates RWX for sandboxing suspicious code. The AV engine itself may produce 10-15 malfind hits legitimately. HOWEVER: (1) 29 is ~2x the AV-elevated baseline — still a significant excess; (2) the CROSS-SERVER CORRELATION with admin server (31 RWX, different kernel base, different server role, confirmed MALICE) eliminates the AV-specific false-positive hypothesis; (3) no legitimate AV configuration produces near-identical RWX counts to a non-AV admin server; (4) concurrent persistent cmd.exe shells (F-001) independently confirm compromise.
findings.corroboration: CONFIRMED by F-001 (nocturnal cmd.exe C2). EXTERNALLY CORROBORATED by VIGIA-REAL-SRL-ADMIN: 31 RWX processes from same framework, different machine (kernel base 0xf8032461e000 vs 0xf80001a06000). Cross-case framework fingerprint match.

habit_incongruence.confirmed_by: Cross-server framework fingerprint (29 vs 31) + F-001 corroboration + AV targeting = T1562.001

findings.title: AV server network connections — endpoint telemetry exposure

peirce_chain.firstness: Active TCP connections from AV server to internal domain infrastructure at time of acquisition.
peirce_chain.secondness: AV servers maintain extensive legitimate connections: agent heartbeats from managed endpoints, signature distribution, policy updates, quarantine sync, console management. Without specific C2 IP/port, AV management traffic is indistinguishable from attacker operations.
peirce_chain.thirdness: In context of confirmed compromise (F-001 + F-002), the attacker has visibility into all AV telemetry — they can see what the AV detects across every managed endpoint. This strategic intelligence enables targeted evasion. However, the specific connections are not differentiated from legitimate AV operations.
